old: A European port city once forced incoming ships to sit offshore for a set stretch of time before anyone could disembark.
Venice imposed this on ships from plague-affected ports in the 1300s — specifically, a wait of exactly forty days.
The Italian phrase behind it literally means “forty days”; quarter and quart are distant cousins, both from the Latin word for four.
clues: This public health measure once lasted exactly forty days, the wait Venice imposed on ships from plague-affected ports before anyone could come ashore.
Today it means any enforced separation to stop a disease spreading, however long it lasts. Unlike isolation of the already sick, it often applies to people merely exposed.
During a pandemic, arriving travelers might be ordered into two weeks of hotel ___. The word is a distant cousin of quarter and quart, all from Latin for four.
